newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan child murderer arrested for another killing.
newsitem.headline: Japan child murderer arrested for another killing.

text.p: A 15-year-old boy in custody for the beheading murder of a playmate was arrested again on Tuesday for three more attacks on schoolchildren, including the suspected murder of a 10-year-old girl.

The boy, whose name was withheld because he is a minor, is suspected of striking a 10-year-old girl on the back of her head with a hammer at around noon on March 16, a police spokesman told reporters. The girl died a week later.
The spokesman said about 15 minutes later, police suspect the boy stabbed and seriously wounded a nine-year-old girl.
The boy has also been linked to a hammer attack in February on two primary school girls in which one of them was slightly injured, the spokesman said.
All of the attacks, including the beheading murder in May, took place in the western Japan port city of Kobe.
On June 28, the boy, then aged 14, was arrested on suspicion of murdering and beheading Jun Hase, an 11-year-old playmate.
Under the new arrest order, the boy can be detained in custody for another 20 days for further questioning.
Hase's brutal killing, which shocked a nation that prides itself on being a safe society, forced patrols for weeks to accompany children to school until the boy's arrest.
The severed head was found at the gate of the suspect's junior high school. A note stuck in the mouth said the murderer was taking revenge on Japan's rigid education system.
Japanese media reports said the boy told police the earlier attacks on the schoolgirls were trial runs for Hase's killing.
"I simply wanted to try out various methods of killing," NHK public television quoted the suspect as telling investigators.

In the suspect's room, police found horror-movie videos and books on past murder cases, such as the U.S. serial killer of the 1960s named the "Zodiac Killer", whose letters to police were mimicked in a note the killer sent to the Japanese media.
Media reports have said the boy has confessed to all the attacks, including showing police a pond in which he threw a hammer, knife and saw used to decapitate Hase.
The weapons have all been recovered by police divers.
The reports said the boy, who has a history of beheading animals including cats and pigeons, shoplifted the weapons so they could not be traced to him.
Kyodo news agency said the boy's lawyers planned to challenge the new arrest order and length of time he is having to spend in custody before a decision is taken on his future.
Under-age criminals are tried by Family Courts where there are no traditional prosecution proceedings and the emphasis is on rehabilitation rather than punishment.

"Detention over the long term is a problem, even though this is an extraordinary case," Kyodo quoted one of the boy's lawyers as saying. "And what is more worrying is that this will become a precedent for other juvenile cases, and lead to long-term detentions becoming common."
If convicted of the beheading and other attacks, the suspect faces a maximum sentence of just two years at a juvenile correction centre.
